    • Term You May HearIt Actually Means...
    • One-Line ExplanationSoC / Chip

    The brain and heart of the phone

    The core component that determines how fast the phone is and whether games lag. RAM (Memory) Phone's "short-term work desk"
    The bigger the desk, the more apps can run simultaneously, and switching between them is smoother. ROM (Storage) Phone's "large warehouse"
    Where photos, videos, and apps are stored. 128GB, 256GB refers to this. OLED / LCD Two types of screen materials
    OLED has richer colors and saves more power; LCD is easier on the eyes and costs less. NFC Near-field wireless communication
    The "tap" feature that lets your phone transform into a transit card, access card, or bank card. OTA Update Over-the-air system upgrade
    That "System Update" button you tap in [Settings]—that's it. Root Android super administrator privileges
    Once obtained, you can modify system files, but there are risks involved. BL Lock Bootloader Lock
    A security lock added by manufacturers; it must be unlocked before flashing custom firmware. NPU Neural Processing Unit
    A chip dedicated to handling AI tasks—dozens of times faster than CPU with lower power consumption. On-Device AI AI running locally on the phone
    AI runs directly on the phone without needing internet connection—fast speed and good privacy. Qi2 Next-generation wireless charging standard
    Wireless charging with magnetic positioning, similar to MagSafe—more convenient charging. eSIM Embedded SIM Card
    A SIM card without a physical card—written directly into the phone. Switch carriers without changing cards. LTPO Adaptive refresh rate technology

    Appendix F: Foldable Phone Purchasing and Usage Special Topic

    Currently, there are two mainstream categories:

    Horizontal Folding (Book-style)

    : When closed, it's the size of a regular phone; when opened, it's nearly square like a small tablet. Representatives: Huawei Mate X series, Samsung Galaxy Z Fold series, Xiaomi MIX Fold series, vivo X Fold series. Main selling point: "one phone = phone + tablet".Vertical Folding (Clamshell-style): When closed, it looks like a compact powder case; when opened, it's a normal-sized phone. Representatives: Huawei Pocket series, Samsung Galaxy Z Flip series, OPPO Find N Flip, Xiaomi MIX Flip. Main selling point: "compact portability + cover screen quick view".

    Key advancements in 2024-2025: Hinge lifespan is generally rated at 500,000 folds (opening/closing 100 times daily lasts 13 years), UTG ultra-thin glass has replaced early plastic films, creases are visible to the naked eye but barely perceptible by touch, prices have dropped from the 10,000+ yuan range down to the 5,000-6,000 yuan range.

    • One-Sentence VerdictIf your current slab phone fully meets your needs and you have no pain point of "screen not being big enough," don't buy a foldable. It's a "nice-to-have" device, not a "must-have" device.
    • II. Who Should Buy a Foldable Phone?Based on real user feedback, these groups have a high probability of finding foldables "worth it":

    Key advances in 2024-2026: hinge life generally rated at 500,000 folds (100 folds/day for 13 years), UTG ultra-thin glass replacing early plastic films, creases visible but barely felt by touch, prices dropping from the 10,000 yuan tier to 4,000-5,000 yuan.

    : Frequently view PDFs, annotate documents, and read long articles on their phone. When unfolded, the ~7.5-inch inner screen lets you view A4 PDFs without zooming—a transformative experience.

    Frequent Travelers / Business Users

    : Don't want to carry a tablet but find phone screens too small. Horizontal foldables let you view PPTs, sign contracts, and compare emails side-by-side—significantly more efficient than a slab phone.

    Creatives Who Love "Flex Mode"

    1. : Fold to 90° and place on a desk—upper screen for framing, lower screen for shutter (selfies/timelapse); upper screen video, lower screen notes; upper screen livestream, lower screen comments—a form factor slab phones simply cannot achieve.Female Users Who Want Portability + Big Screen
    2. : Vertical foldables fit into small bags when closed, unfold to normal phone size, and the cover screen can serve as a makeup mirror or notification viewer.These People Should NOT Buy One
    3. If you only use your phone for short videos, WeChat, and calling—foldables offer zero benefit and are heavier and thicker instead.If you have small hands or wrist tendonitis—horizontal foldables weigh 230g+ when unfolded, making single-handed use tiring.
    4. If you're on a tight budget and plan to keep a phone for 4+ years—foldables have lower resale value than slab phones, and repair costs are high.III. Buying Guide: Check These 6 Metrics

    Don't get dazzled by the word "folding"—focus on these key points when shopping:

    • Hinge Type
    • : Waterdrop hinge (shallower crease, longer lifespan, currently mainstream) is better than U-type hinge (deeper crease, early solution). Ask sales staff or check reviews to confirm which type.
    • Inner Screen Material

    : Must be UTG ultra-thin glass, not early plastic film. UTG feels close to glass; plastic film feels indented under fingernails and easily retains marks.

    Crease Performance

    • : Go to a store and unfold it yourself. The 2025 qualified standard: almost invisible head-on with screen on, visible as a shallow groove under angled light, slight depression when finger runs across but not sharp.Cover Screen Size
    • : For horizontal foldables, the larger the outer screen the better (ideally 6.4"+) so it works as a normal phone when closed; for vertical foldables, larger is more practical (4"+ allows replying to messages and viewing navigation).Weight & Thickness
    • : Horizontal foldables at 230-260g unfolded is normal; under 230g is excellent. Closed thickness of 12-14mm; under 12mm is thin. Vertical foldables must fit comfortably in a shirt pocket when closed to qualify.: Go to a physical store and unfold it yourself. The 2026 acceptable standard is: almost invisible when screen is on, a shallow groove visible under angled light, slight depression when fingers pass over but not sharp.
    • : Focus on inner screen crack repair cost. Some brands offer free inner screen replacement once in the first year; others charge 2,000-4,000 yuan out-of-pocket. This is the biggest hidden cost of owning a foldable.In-Store Experience Checklist
    • Open and close it 10 times yourself—feel if the hinge damping is smooth and if there are any unusual sounds.Unfold it and look at the crease under angled light, then look at it head-on with the screen on.
    • Hold it single-handed in unfolded state for 30 seconds—feel if the weight is acceptable.Try Flex Mode: fold to 90°, place on desk, try taking photos and watching videos.

    Ask clearly about the standalone inner screen repair price and warranty policy.

    1. IV. Unique Foldable Usage Tips
    2. After buying one, here are experiences you can't get with a slab phone:
    3. 1. Split-Screen & Multitasking
    4. When a horizontal foldable is unfolded, most systems support top/bottom or left/right split-screen. Typical scenarios: upper screen for online course video, lower screen for notes; left side WeChat, right side documents; upper screen map navigation, lower screen music. Much more practical than slab phone split-screens because the screen is large enough that neither half feels cramped.
    5. 2. Flex Mode (90° Fold)

    This is the "killer feature" usage of foldables:

    Selfies / Group Photos

    : Place on desk folded to 90°, upper screen for framing, lower screen for shutter—no need to ask someone else to take the photo.

    Timelapse / Night Shots

    : Same stable placement on desk—saves you from needing a tripod.

    Video Calls

    • : Frees both hands; the other person sees you from a more natural angle too.Watching Videos
    • : Use as a mini TV on a desk—especially practical on airplane/high-speed rail tray tables.Cover Screen Preview + Inner Screen Shooting
    • : When using the rear camera to shoot yourself, the cover screen displays the live preview for more accurate composition.3. Cover Screen Quick View
    • When a vertical foldable is closed, the cover screen can: show time/notifications/weather, reply to WeChat (voice-to-text or quick replies), tap transit cards, view navigation, act as a makeup mirror (using front camera). No need to unfold every time—saves power and effort.4. Desktop Mode
    • Some horizontal foldables (Huawei, Samsung) can switch to "Desktop Mode" when unfolded. After connecting an external display, keyboard, and mouse, it works like a basic PC—adequate for temporary document processing and email replies. Not a primary productivity tool, but great for emergencies.V. Maintenance Tips: Help Your Foldable Last Longer
    The most delicate parts of a foldable are the inner screen and hinge. These habits can significantly extend its lifespan:

    Don't Force Open/Close in Low Temperatures

    : Below 0°C, UTG glass becomes brittle. Warm it in your pocket for a few minutes before opening/closing. This is something written in every official manual but nobody reads.

    Avoid Nails/Hard Objects Touching the Inner Screen

    : The inner screen has a protective layer but is softer than the outer screen. Operate with your fingertips, never poke with fingernails.

    Check for Foreign Objects Before Closing

    • : A single grain of sand caught inside when closing could directly crush the inner screen. Glance over it before closing.Don't Apply Regular Tempered Glass Film
    • : The inner screen can only use official specialized film or UTG protective film. Regular tempered glass film affects folding and touch functionality. Recommend going to official after-sales for screen protector application.Keep Dust & Liquids Away from the Hinge
    • : Although most claim IPX8 water resistance, dust resistance ratings are generally low. Be careful at beaches, construction sites, etc.Apply Even Force When Opening/Closing
    • : Don't violently flick it open with one hand. Opening smoothly with both hands from the center is most stable.High-Risk Scenarios for Inner Screen Damage
    • Catching headphone/charging cable when closing—directly cracks the inner screen.Mixing with keys in a bag—outer screen fine, but keys press creases into the inner screen.
    • Immediately opening/closing when moving from cold outdoors to warm indoors in winter—temperature difference causes glass stress changes.After a year of use, feeling "the crease got deeper" and trying to peel off the factory film—peeling the film will damage the inner screen along with it.

    VI. Foldable "Pitfalls" & Realistic Expectations

    • Before buying, keep these things in mind:
    • The Crease Will Always Be There
    • : 2025 technology cannot achieve "completely invisible"—only "almost invisible head-on with screen on". If you're a perfectionist who would stare at the crease uncomfortably every day, don't buy.
    • Heavier & Thicker

    : Horizontal foldables weigh 230g+ when unfolded—more tiring for single-handed use than slab phones. Closed thickness of 12-14mm makes pockets bulge more.

    Battery Life Is Generally Average

    • : Because space must accommodate the hinge mechanism, battery capacity is compressed. At the same price point, battery life typically falls short of slab phones.: 2026 technology can't achieve "completely crease-free" — only "almost invisible from the front when screen is on." If you're a perfectionist who'll be bothered by the crease daily, don't buy.
    • : After one year, the second-hand price is usually 50-60% of the new phone price—drops faster than slab phones.Expensive Repairs
    • : Inner screen assembly repair costs 2,000-4,000 yuan; hinge repair costs 500-1,500 yuan. Check warranty policies clearly before buying.Inconsistent App Adaptation
    • : Mainstream apps have adapted to large screens, but niche apps may just be "stretched/enlarged" with mediocre experience.A foldable is not a "better phone"—it's "a phone in a different form factor." Buy it because you need its unique form, not because it's "more advanced."
    • —— On the Philosophy of Choosing a Foldable PhoneVII. How to Choose Among Mainstream Brands (2025)

    Conclusion: Stay Curious, Stay Clear-Headed

    Congratulations on making it this far.

    This book covers everything from phone hardware to software ecosystem, from daily settings to developer mode, from security protection to digital legacy. If it helped you solve one practical problem — even just learning to turn off an unnecessary permission or forming a backup habit — then these words weren't written in vain.

    But more important than any specific technique are two things:

    • Stay Curious: Phones change every year, AI is changing, foldable screens are changing, satellite communication is changing. The operation steps you learn today may be outdated tomorrow, but the curiosity of "wanting to know why" never goes out of date. Asking one more question — "What does this permission do?" "Where is this data stored?" "Could this feature leak privacy?" — is more useful than memorizing a hundred operation steps.
    • Stay Clear-Headed: The phone is a tool, not a master. It's designed to capture your attention, occupy your time, and guide your consumption. Using it is your choice; being used by it is your loss of control. Periodically check your screen time, and think "Am I using my phone to get things done, or is my phone consuming me?" — this isn't melodrama, it's a survival instinct in the digital age.

    Technology changes, but human needs don't — we need security, connection, and respect. The phone is just a medium. The real "phone class" isn't in a book — it's in the moment you unlock your screen every day.

    One Last Exercise

    Close this book, pick up your phone, and do one thing:Take 30 seconds to think: what three things in your phone would you "truly regret losing"?Then, make sure they're backed up. This book was worth it.

    This book is still being updated. Below are the planned directions for future versions — and feel free to tell us in your feedback what you'd most like to see.

    From the paradigm shift of AI coding, the five thinking principles, context and requirements engineering, the 2026 landscape of tools and models, hands-on API practice, conversation engineering, three complete projects, quality assurance, and the road to more advanced skills — taking you from “knowing how to use AI” up to “directing AI to write code”; to the complete development pipeline for the two big platforms, Android and iOS: environment setup (Android Studio / Xcode), language crash courses (Kotlin / Swift), UI frameworks (Jetpack Compose / SwiftUI), data and networking, hands-on projects (an expense tracker + a weather app), testing and publishing (Google Play / App Store), and a quick-reference handbook — taking you all the way from everyday digital user to app developer.

    A note on timeliness

    Phone technology moves extremely fast, and this book was written based on the technology and market conditions of mid-2026. AI capabilities, chip models, system versions, and price ranges may all have changed by the time you read this. For specific step-by-step instructions, go by the actual system version on your device; for purchasing decisions, check the latest reviews and user feedback.
